title: A new idempotency key is minted for every click, so a retry after an unconfirmed refund is not deduplicated
evidence: app.js:119-137 generates the key inside refundSelected on each click and does not keep it. On error the catch at app.js:131-133 leaves state.selected intact and the finally at app.js:135-136 re-enables the button. README.md:9 makes the server's only protection against a double refund the Idempotency-Key header; api.js:32 says the key covers 'the same attempt'. Traced; the server was not available to run.
failing_case: The user selects 3 orders and clicks Refund, then confirms. The server processes the refund but the response is lost (504 from a proxy, a dropped connection, or a 200 with an empty body, which request() turns into 'not valid JSON'). The UI shows 'The refund was not confirmed.', keeps the 3 rows ticked and re-enables the Refund button. The user clicks Refund again. refundSelected calls newIdempotencyKey() again, so the server sees a different key and refunds the same 3 orders a second time. The only guard is a sentence telling the user to check first.
remediation: Create the key once per intent (when the selection is confirmed) and reuse it for every retry of the same ids until the server gives a definite answer. Keep the pending attempt in state, and after an ambiguous failure reload the orders and disable rows whose status already changed instead of offering the same refund again.

title: Orders that are already refunded or still pending can be selected and sent for refund
evidence: renderRow (app.js:34-60) creates an enabled checkbox for every status, and the Refund button is gated only on refunding, loading and selection count (app.js:83). No eligibility rule exists in domain.js. README.md:7-8 assigns only 'may this user refund' and the idempotency key to the server, not 'is this order refundable'.
failing_case: Set Status to 'refunded', tick a row, click Refund selected, confirm the dialog 'This sends money back to the customers.' A POST /api/v1/refunds goes out for an order that is already refunded. If the server does not reject it, money is paid out twice. If it rejects it, the user sees a generic 'refund was not confirmed' failure for an action the UI should never have offered.
remediation: Add a pure isRefundable(order) to domain.js (status === 'paid'), disable the checkbox for other statuses, filter picked through it in refundSelected, and state in the README that the server also enforces it.

requirement.why: A refund control that accepts already-refunded orders contradicts the 'refunded' status the page itself displays; the README names no eligibility rule.

title: normaliseOrder turns a null, empty-string or empty-array total into $0.00 instead of rejecting the record
evidence: The comment at domain.js:7 says the record is dropped when there is 'no numeric total', but Number(null), Number("") and Number([]) are all 0, which passes Number.isFinite at domain.js:12. Traced from JS semantics; the Bash tool refused node, so no run.
failing_case: The API returns { id: 'A7', total: null, status: 'pending', customer: {...} }. The row is shown with a Total of $0.00, counts in the Orders stat, and is not counted in 'skipped', so no 'data is incomplete' note appears. If the user ticks it, the confirm dialog at app.js:123 states a refund 'totalling $0.00' while the server refunds the real, unknown amount.
remediation: Accept only typeof raw.total === 'number' or a non-empty numeric string, and return null otherwise so the skipped counter reports it. Add a unit test for null, '', [] and true.

title: The Revenue card re-applies tax and a gold discount to the server's total, so it matches nothing in the table
evidence: orderRevenueCents (domain.js:25-30) multiplies each paid order's total by 1.0825, and by 0.9 first for gold customers. The table column (app.js:51) and the refund amount (app.js:122) use the raw total. No document says order.total is pre-tax or pre-discount. summarise is the only caller (app.js:28). Traced; arithmetic recomputed by hand (10000 cents x 10825/10000 = 10825; gold 9000 x 10825/10000 = 9742.5, rounds to 9743).
failing_case: One paid standard-tier order with total 100.00 shows Total $100.00 in the table and Revenue $108.25 in the card. One paid gold order with total 100.00 shows $100.00 and $97.43. A refund of that order would send $100.00 back. If the server's total already includes tax and discount, the card is overstated or understated by 8.25% or more on every order, and the number finance reads is wrong.
remediation: Have the server return the revenue figures (or a documented net/gross field per order) and display them. If the rule must live on the client, document what total means, keep it in domain.js with a test, and label the card with what it includes.

requirement.why: The card is labelled Revenue next to a Total column; nothing states that totals are net of tax or that revenue is grossed up.

title: HTTP failures show 'The server answered 401 Unauthorized.' with no cause or next step
evidence: All non-2xx statuses become one message. app.js:108 and app.js:133 print it verbatim. The app relies on a session cookie (api.js:1-2), so expiry is the ordinary 401/403 case.
failing_case: The session expires. The user searches and sees 'Orders could not be loaded. The server answered 401 Unauthorized.' They are not told to sign in again. A refund shows 'The refund was not confirmed. The server answered 403 Forbidden. Reload and check…' and a reload only produces another 401.
remediation: Map 401 to 'Your session has ended. Sign in again.', 403 to 'You do not have permission to do this.', and 5xx to 'The server had a problem. Try again in a minute.'

title: The page heading is 24px left of the content column at wide widths
evidence: main is max-width 1100px with 24px padding (styles.css:24), so its content starts 24px inside the 1100 box. The h1 has the same 1100px max width and no padding. At 1360px wide: h1 starts at x=130, main content at x=154. At 390px both start at 24px, so only wide screens misalign.
failing_case: Open at 1360px: 'Orders' starts 24px to the left of the stat tiles and the table below it.
remediation: Give the h1 padding: 0 24px with box-sizing border-box (and header padding 20px 0), or share one .container class between header and main.
